summary: US-P4: The sale charges the resolved price, and the reservation records why
description:
**As** a buyer, **I want** the price I was quoted to be the price I am charged, **so that** a rule change mid-checkout never moves the number under me — and **as** the organizer, I want to be able to prove afterwards which rule produced it.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-151 (resolution + provenance exist)

Closes the epic by putting the hierarchy on the money path. Today `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go` reads catalog's `/internal/ticket-types/{id}` and takes `price.amount` verbatim; after this story it takes the **resolved** price and persists the provenance alongside the reservation.

**⚠️ Money path.** Anticipated and in scope for this ticket — but the plan must say explicitly which existing money invariants it preserves.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Commerce's reserve path sources `unit_amount` from catalog's rules resolution instead of the raw ticket-type price. With **no rules defined the behaviour is byte-identical to today** — the existing commerce and smoke tests stay green unmodified, and that is the regression proof.
- [ ] The reservation persists the **provenance** of the price it was created with (winning rule id + scope level + active tier), so a completed order can be traced to the rule that priced it.
- [ ] **The quote is pinned to the hold**: the price resolved at reserve time is the price checkout charges. A test changes the rules between reserve and checkout and proves the reservation's amount does not move.
- [ ] Resolution failure **fails closed** (ADR-028): a malformed, drifted, or unreachable resolution response aborts the reserve with an error — it never silently falls back to the base price. Note the distinction the test must encode: *no rule matched* is a valid 200 answering with the base price; *could not resolve* is not.
- [ ] Money stays integer minor units end to end (ADR-001); the existing overflow guard on `unit_amount × quantity` still holds for a rule-supplied amount.
- [ ] The commerce operation is exercised through the running stack in the smoke suite (ADR-030 — commerce **is** in the happy-path coverage gate, unlike catalog), and OpenAPI/`api-types.gen.ts` are regenerated and committed before the gate runs.

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002); money is integer minor units + ISO-4217 code, floats banned (ADR-001).

objective.note: A pricing hierarchy nothing sells through is inert; this is the ticket that makes TKT-5 real, and it makes the sale auditable.

scope.note: IN: reserve-path price sourcing, provenance persistence, quote pinning, fail-closed. OUT: repricing on exchange/refund (TKT-9), fees (TKT-6), cart/multi-item (TKT-8), storefront display of provenance.

uncertainties.note: Whether provenance is a column set or a jsonb blob on `reservations` is a Planning-time call; both are reversible within one migration.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-151. Runs after TKT-152 in this epic's sequence, but does not depend on it — the pinning AC holds whether or not tiers exist.

approach.note: Swap the catalog call in commerce's reserve handler for the resolution endpoint; new commerce migration adds provenance columns to `reservations`; the pinning AC is proven at the API test seam with a fake catalog, plus the smoke suite end-to-end.

first_slice.note: One vertical path: reserve → resolved price → persisted provenance → checkout charges the pinned amount.

success.note: Epic COS-1's 'visible provenance' becomes durable, not just readable.

context_memo.note: Baked below; governingAdrs resolved from docs/adr/ at 2026-07-30 and to be re-resolved at claim time.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.
Every money mutation flows through the append-only journal; every price/fee decision resolves through the rules hierarchy (TKT-5) once it exists.

governingAdrs.why: DID NOT EXIST when this mémo was baked. §6 is the load-bearing part for this ticket: catalog is the SINGLE authority for the rule-resolved unit price, and commerce consumes resolved_price WITHOUT recomputing it. §5 is the provenance shape to persist — frozen deliberately across TKT-151/152 so snapshots span one format.

AMENDED by ADR-036 on the pricing row. The mémo's original entry ('commerce owns pricing evaluation') is now WRONG for this ticket. Commerce owns sale-time COMPOSITION — price + fees + promos + taxes into an order total — not resolution.

Fail closed. A resolution response commerce cannot validate must abort the reserve, never degrade to the base price. Note the distinction the tests must encode: 'no rule matched' is a valid 200 answering with the base price; 'could not resolve' is not.
The claim/hold transaction is inventory's. Commerce supplies unit_amount to /holds; do not move pricing into the contention path.
The checkout journal protocol governs what commerce records at checkout. Provenance is added ALONGSIDE journalled facts, never in place of one.

Checkout recovery: reserve→checkout is resumable, so anything persisted at reserve time must survive and be RE-READ on the recovery path rather than re-derived — which is also what makes the quote pinning real.
Commerce IS inside the smoke happy-path coverage gate (unlike catalog). A new or changed documented 2xx operation must be exercised through the running stack or the suite fails.
Integer minor units end to end; the existing overflow guard on unit_amount × quantity must still hold for a rule-supplied amount.
Regenerate and COMMIT openapi_gen.go / api-types.gen.ts before the gate.
A commerce migration runs out-of-band via that binary's migrate subcommand.
If the plan calls the stored provenance auditable: name the adversary. It is honest-writer consistency, not tamper-evidence — ADR-036 §3 has the wording to reuse.

reference.summary: The seam to change: `reserve()` in services/commerce/internal/api/server.go calls `/internal/ticket-types/{id}` and uses `o.Price.Amount` for both the hold and the reservation row.
`reservations.unit_amount` / `total_amount` are the columns the resolved price lands in (commerce migration 0001).

TKT-154 records two pre-existing ticket_types gaps (price_amount unbounded, currency case) that make a legal row unreturnable by a contract-declared endpoint. Not this ticket's to fix, but the reserve path reads that row.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-153 (⚠️ money path)

**Gate 1 waived** (epic TKT-5's `kind=claim`). Last child of the epic; TKT-151 (its only blocker)
and TKT-152 both closed.

**Selection reason.** The only remaining claimable ticket, and deliberately taken **last**: it is
the one that puts the pricing model on a real sale, and it is better done against a finished model
than a half-finished one. TKT-152's windows now exist, so the provenance TKT-153 persists is the
final shape rather than one that gains fields a ticket later.

**Not `risk:low`, and this is the ticket where the run's stop conditions get their real test.**

#### The money-path trigger, and why it does not fire

The run's instructions say to stop if implementation would touch **money paths** *"in a way the
ticket and plan did not anticipate"*. This ticket changes how a sale is priced — that is a money
path by any reading. It does **not** trip the condition, because it is the anticipated one:

- the epic's decomposition named it as a money path and flagged it as concern 2 in the readiness
  verdict, before any code existed;
- the ticket's own ACs are written around the risk — *"with no rules defined the behaviour is
  byte-identical to today, and the existing commerce and smoke tests stay green unmodified"* is the
  regression proof, stated up front;
- ADR-036 §6 already decided the boundary this change respects.

**What WOULD trip it, and where I will stop:** pricing work spilling into payment
authorization/capture, the settlement ledger, the NF525 journal, or the refund/exchange paths. None
of those is in scope, and if the implementation starts reaching for them I stop and report rather
than widening a money-path diff on my own authority.

#### Context-mémo revalidated at pickup

Baked at decomposition (`capturedAt: 2026-07-30`). Everything material has changed since: **ADR-036
now exists** (it did not when this mémo was written) and has been amended three times; **ADR-002 was
amended** by it on exactly the row this ticket depends on. `governingAdrs` rewritten below.

The mémo's original ADR-002 line said *commerce owns pricing evaluation*. **That is now wrong in the
direction that matters most for this ticket** — catalog resolves the unit price; commerce composes
the order total and consumes `resolved_price` without recomputing it.

#### Where this ticket's ACs stand

**Unchanged.** Unlike TKT-151 and TKT-152, no AC needed re-syncing: this ticket was written against
the sale path, and nothing the spike or the two catalog stories decided contradicts it. The one
sharpening worth noting is that "provenance" now has a concrete, frozen shape (`PriceResolution`),
so *"persists the provenance"* means storing that object rather than inventing a format.

Branch: `TKT-153-sale-uses-resolved-price`.
